Priya S: Heads up — customer reported duplicate tokens billed when their client reconnects within ~1-3s after an SSE disconnect. Looks like we re-sent the last partial chunk on resume and the billing pipeline counted it twice. Anyone seen this pattern?
Alex K: Seen something similar in logs last week. Resume arrives, we replay buffered chunk, but downstream billing sandbox doesn't dedupe based on resume-id.
Jordan L: Is this happening only for SSE or websockets too? Could be tied to how we commit "consumed" markers on connection close vs ack from downstream.
Priya S: Mostly SSE so far. Customer uses short messages, so the duplicate chunk is small but still charged. They pasted headers: `Resume-ID: r_7f3b`, `X-Stream-Lease: 12s`.
Mei C: Quick idea: require a resume-ack handshake before we forward replayed bytes to billing. Server would buffer replayed bytes and only mark them billable once client ack's receipt of resume frame.
Sam G: That sounds safer. But it changes latency on resume and is a behavioral rollback. Also affects our billing SLOs. Console UX needs to show "pending-resume" tokens if we hold billing until ack.
Alex K: Agree. Alternative: attach `resume-id` metadata to billed events and have billing dedupe on (tenant, resume-id, offset). Less UX impact but requires billing infra change.
Jordan L: Billing team may not want to do cross-service dedupe at that granularity. We should prefer a runtime change that avoids duplicate emission.
Priya S: Also telemetry issue: Console shows token counts spike but request->tokens telemetry doesn't show resume metadata. That's why support gets confused. We should include resume-id and replay-flag in traces.
Mei C: Minimal steps: 1) runtime: tag replayed bytes with `replay=true` 2) streaming ingress: don't increment "billed_tokens" metric until either (a) client ack on resume frame or (b) 5s passthrough fallback. 3) console: new column in per-route billing trace for "replayed_pending" tokens.
Sam G: If we choose ack path, we need a small protocol change: after `:resume` event server sends `:resume-ack resume-id` frame. Client SDKs must surface it (websocket and SSE). We can gate it behind a rollout flag.
Alex K: Implementation note: we already have `Resume-ID` in headers. Add `X-Resume-Ack: yes` as a lightweight frame. Runtime can buffer per-connection kv for up to `X-Stream-Lease` seconds.
Jordan L: Edgecases: client disconnects before ack -> we must expire buffer and then mark tokens as billed to avoid revenue leakage. Need a conservative timeout (lease) and metric to track expirations.
Priya S: Good point. Also routing policy: if resume routes to a different shard (due to sticky routing TTL), we might not find buffer. That causes the replay to be fully emitted again — the exact bug. We need resume routing affinity or a fallback that routes resume to last-serving shard for lease window.
Mei C: Could implement short-lived sticky cookie: route-key = `last-node:<resume-id>` with TTL=lease. Router would prefer that for resume requests. Simple and avoids cross-shard state.
Sam G: Does that play well with Dedicated customers? Sticky routing needs to respect tenant isolation; fine as long as shard is in the same pool.
Alex K: Console/rollout UX: we should add a toggle in Rollouts that enables "resume-ack" behavior per env so we can canary it for customers who care about dedupe. Also a telemetry flag to correlate before/after token deltas.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: runtime/resume-buffer v1 -> r1 cluster at 2026-03-20T11:02:30Z
Priya S: Action items: @Alex K prototype buffered replay + resume-ack handshake (canary). @Mei C add resume-id and replay flag to telemetry spans. @Sam G coordinate with billing for short-term dedupe opt-in if needed. I'll open a ticket with logs and a minimal repro.
Alex K: I'll put a small reproducible curl example in the ticket: e.g. `curl -H "Resume-ID: r_foo" -H "X-Stream-Lease: 8" ...` and a tiny SSE client that disconnects after partial chunk.
Jordan L: Also add unit test for cross-shard resume where router prefers sticky route. I can take that.
Priya S: Thanks folks. Let's try to keep the behavior opt-in until billing confirms no regressions. :thumbsup:
